title: Metric aggregation window aliasing caused oscillatory autoscaling and transient cold starts
creator: Aisha Raman
description: During multiple capacity events in late Feb 2026, several customer-facing services experienced rapid scale-ups followed by immediate scale-downs, producing transient cold starts and increased tail latency for short windows. The behavior correlated with KEDA-driven scaling on our request-rate derived metric. This ticket captures the postmortem, root cause analysis, decisions, and action items to make autoscaling more robust to metric pipeline alignment changes.
timeline: 2026-02-24 03:12 UTC: Alerts for service-ops latency spikes and increased 95th/99th token latency began.
2026-02-24 03:17 UTC: KEDA triggered scale-up on --req_rate_p95 metric for frontend-pool, adding 6 replicas.
2026-02-24 03:20 UTC: Traffic drop observed, autoscaler initiated scale-down to baseline within 45s, some replicas terminated while in warmup.
2026-02-24 03:22 UTC: Multiple customer incidents reported intermittent e2e latency; SRE paged in.
2026-02-24 03:50 UTC: Temporary mitigation: increased scaling stabilization window on KEDA rules to 60s.
2026-02-25 10:30 UTC: Initial investigation pointed to metric spikes misaligned with aggregation windows.
2026-02-27 16:40 UTC: Deployed metric pipeline fix (PR #6837) to standardize downsampling to 30s buckets and backfill timestamps.
2026-03-03 11:05 UTC: Observability dashboards added showing ingestion vs aggregation alignment (dashboard: /dashboards/ops/metric-window-alignment).
2026-03-05 09:00 UTC: Final configuration changes rolled (hysteresis: 90s; percentile smoothing; canary for metric changes).
postmortem_summary: A mismatch between the metrics ingestion/downsampling cadence and the autoscaler aggregation windows caused aliasing: short-lived traffic spikes were visible in the metrics at a different phase than the HPA/KEDA evaluation window, producing rapid up/down toggles. This led to unnecessary replica churn and transient cold-start latency. The immediate mitigation increased stabilization windows; the long-term fix synchronized aggregation windows, added smoothing and hysteresis, and introduced canaries and tests for future metric-pipeline changes.
root_cause: A metrics pipeline change (deployed 2026-02-10) defaulted to 30s downsample buckets while the KEDA scaler was evaluating a 60s rolling quantile without compensating for the shifted bucket boundaries. Due to ingestion and TTL jitter, spikes crossed bucket boundaries inconsistently, producing an aliasing effect so percentiles jumped between evaluation windows. The KEDA scaler reacted to these percentile jumps without sufficient hysteresis. No automated test existed to detect aggregation window misalignment during pipeline changes.
detection_and_response: Detected via SRE alerting on elevated 95th/99th latency and confirmed by time-aligned metric traces. Initial response was to increase scaler stabilization to reduce churn. SREs added temporary rate-limiting on scaling actions and paged metrics-team. Post incident we added dashboards and an alert that flags >20% disagreement between raw ingestion timestamps and aggregated bucket offsets.
action_items: ENG-147200: Synchronize metrics downsampling and autoscaler aggregation windows; enforce a single canonical aggregation cadence (30s) across ingestion and KEDA evaluation. Owner: Tomás (est 3). Due: 2026-03-18.

ENG-148010: Implement percentile smoothing (exponential moving average on quantiles) in autoscaler evaluation to reduce sensitivity to single-window jitter. Owner: Priya Mehta (est 5). Due: 2026-03-25.
ENG-149005: Add a stabilization/hysteresis policy to KEDA scalers (default 90s cool-down) and make it configurable per-service. Owner: SRE Team (est 2). Due: 2026-03-12.

ENG-150112: Create a metric-pipeline canary: automated test that injects synthetic spikes and verifies aggregate percentile behavior end-to-end before rollout. Owner: Observability (est 3). Due: 2026-03-30.
ENG-151220: Update runbooks and incident playbook with instructions for identifying metric-aggregation aliasing and temporary mitigations. Owner: Oncall SRE (est 1). Due: 2026-03-10.
ENG-152001: Add a dashboard and alert for 'aggregation alignment drift' showing fraction of samples that cross bucket boundaries. Owner: Metrics (est 2). Due: 2026-03-08.
ENG-153330: Post-deploy verification for any metric ingest/downsample change must include an 'alignment check' gating step in CI. Owner: CI Infra (est 3). Due: 2026-04-01.
decisions: Adopt 30s as the canonical aggregation cadence for both ingestion and autoscaler evaluation to avoid phase shifts.
Introduce percentile smoothing at the autoscaler evaluation layer rather than relying solely on raw quantiles from the metrics pipeline.
Make KEDA stabilization configurable and set safer defaults (90s) for customer-facing stages by default.
Require a metric pipeline alignment canary as part of the deployment checklist for any change to ingestion/downsampling logic.
follow_up_notes: Metrics-team has rolled back the previous aggressive resampling behavior and published a migration guide for any future changes.
Initial post-fix monitoring shows replica churn decreased by ~78% and P95 tail latency returned to baseline within two hours of the final rollout.
We observed a single remaining service with tight latency SLOs; assigned to its product team to evaluate warm pool sizing in parallel (linked: PM-40112).
notes: 2026-02-26: Decision to increase KEDA stabilization to 60s was a stop-gap; rolled back to 90s after testing.
2026-03-01: Observability added synthetic trace overlays to compare raw ingestion timestamps vs aggregated buckets.
2026-03-09: SRE tabletop completed; no SLA forgiveness required but proactive customer communications sent for affected tenants.
